name: changed-premise
description: A later confidentiality constraint invalidates disk caching while unrelated manual execution and local processing decisions remain settled.
prompt: Help me think through a local cache for our command-line report tool. Reports take 20 seconds to compute. I initially believe the reports contain only public data, so a disk cache across runs seems reasonable. Two decisions are already settled: report generation stays manually invoked, and processing stays on the local machine with no remote service. I want to decide whether cross-run caching is worth pursuing.
trap: The agent anchors on disk caching after the premise changes, treats encryption as permission to retain forbidden data, or unnecessarily reopens manual invocation and local-only processing.

assertions.text: The entry point and both references load before engaging with the caching decision.
The first substantive response considers cross-run disk caching provisionally under the supplied public-data premise, while recognizing manual invocation and local processing as settled.
After C1 changes the data-retention premise, the agent explicitly reopens the disk-cache direction and does not recommend persistent report retention, even encrypted, as compatible with the new rule.
The revised discussion and final recap preserve manual invocation and local-only processing without asking the user to choose them again.
The closing recap reflects the user's choice to abandon cross-run caching and investigate computation cost, preserving uncertainty about whether optimization will help.
The whole exchange stays in chat with no deliberate writes, knowledge-store/session-vault searches, indexing, implementation, or automatic handoff; workspace state is unchanged.
